title: Dropbox refresh token placeholders, app key and masked values
summary: An app key and grant type with no refresh token, a token response with no refresh_token member, the documented <REFRESH_TOKEN> placeholder, an environment reference, a template reference and a masked display.
rationale: The app key is the public identifier registered beside the app secret, and a response without a refresh_token member carries no refresh token. A placeholder or reference stands in for a value kept elsewhere, and a masked display has no recoverable value.

expectation.rationale: Project policy, maintainer-only (ADR 0020, credential-evidence#235). Finalized by the sole maintainer alone: not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). The question, options, strongest dissent and reversing evidence are in the review history. Not flagged under project policy: the values here are identifiers, placeholders, references, masked text or non-secret outputs, not credential values. That a placeholder or reference is not a value is a project decision, not a Dropbox statement.

sources.supports: `refresh_token` *String?* A unique, long-lived token that can be used to request new short-lived access tokens without direct interaction from a user in your app.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. All values are synthetic, were built for this record and were not tested against any service. The carrier's existence is what the cited provider pages document; the value admission, span, placeholder handling and attribution are project policy. Parser behaviour, action and product attribution stay with the downstream repositories.
